desc:
Choose two contiguous blocks of nums: one of length exactly a and one of length exactly b. They must not share any index, but they may appear in either order and may touch each other. Return the maximum possible total of the two block sums.

nums = [0, 6, 5, 2, 2, 5, 1, 9, 4], a = 1, b = 2
length-1 block [9] and length-2 block [6,5]: 9 + 11
result = 20
hints: First compute the sum of every window of length a and of length b with prefix sums.
Fix the position where the second window ends. The first window can be any block that ends before the second one starts.
While sweeping, keep the best sum of an a-window seen so far that ends at or before the start of the current b-window. Run the sweep twice, once with a first and once with b first.
editorial: Let P be the prefix sums. Consider the case where the a-window comes before the b-window. Sweep the end i of the b-window; its start is i - b. All a-windows ending at or before i - b are allowed, so maintain their maximum sum as i grows and add the b-window sum P[i] - P[i-b].
Repeat with the roles swapped (b first, then a) and return the larger value. Each sweep is O(n) after the prefix sums, so the total is O(n) time and O(n) space for the prefix array.
